metadata_note: Primary Qwen results repeat all eight answers with waveform-derived question durations; the original question-blind notes are reused unchanged. The earlier eight answers displayed a zero-second text label while receiving the complete waveform; they remain archived. CPU tests verify identical audio and prompts differing only in that duration label. Sampling and runtime variability prevent attributing output differences solely to the label correction.
scope: Two early questions, one meeting each, with two correlated speaker conditions. This is a feasibility pilot, not a model ranking or a 105-question evaluation.
identity_rule: Audio-only answers may identify a speaker by a unique past utterance or a matching audio segment. Labelled examples make A–D available but descriptions are still accepted when uniquely resolvable. No model answer actually used an A–D speaker label.
temporal_rule: The source says Thursday, end of the week, then today or tomorrow. Both time descriptions are accepted for the main-call question.
citation_rule: Answer content and citation correctness are distinct: some Qwen timestamps are malformed, inaccurate or outside the cited evidence; these are not verified temporal grounding.
input_protocol: No oracle transcript or known question text entered either model. All question-blind background states completed before any question was supplied; reactive and notes share the exact full audio history and spoken question within each identity condition.
amortized_generation: Each update receives new audio, up to ten seconds of recent speech, one bounded current note state, and past-only voice examples when applicable. Full state versions are retained on disk. No stacked snapshots.
runtime: One A100 SXM4 80 GB per model, encoder+language model+8 GiB KV on GPU 0, no speech output; models sequential in the audio lane, maximum two GPUs with the separate text lane.
latency: Cold prefix/multimodal caches per request; first-answer time includes reading/preprocessing, audio encoding, prompt processing and exposed native thinking. MiniCPM has no exposed thinking channel.
observed_pattern: Qwen function notes increase request-time thinking in all four matched comparisons; neither voice condition shows a latency reduction. MiniCPM omits timing or overstates file availability in every pilot answer.
